name: North Dakota

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented within 3 months after the first publication and mailing of notice to creditors, or within 3 years after death if notice was not published and mailed (N.D.C.C. § 30.1-19-03(1)).

earliestClose.text: A personal representative may close an unsupervised estate by verified statement, but not until 3 months after the first publication and mailing of notice to creditors (N.D.C.C. § 30.1-21-03).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit if the entire estate subject to succession, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 and no personal representative is pending or appointed (N.D.C.C. § 30.1-23-01). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Affidavit collection up to $100,000 (N.D.C.C. § 30.1-23-01) and summary administration for estates not exceeding allowances and expenses (N.D.C.C. ch. 30.1-23).

filingFee.text: The clerk of district court charges $160 for filing a civil case for decision (N.D.C.C. § 27-05.2-03(1)(a)); a probate-specific fee was not identified in the text read.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (N.D.C.C. § 30.1-18-19).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; the court may review the reasonableness of compensation of persons employed by the personal representative, including attorneys (N.D.C.C. ch. 30.1-18, UPC § 3-721 equivalent).
